QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_10

answer.text: The value of all cash flows beyond the forecast period, often a significant portion of total DCF value

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that DCF uses forecast free cash flows over an explicit forecast period and then adds a perpetual terminal value to capture cash flows accruing after that forecast period. In many cases, terminal value forms the bulk of the enterprise value derived from a DCF. The Trap: Terminal value is not the initial investment, management fees, or liquidation/break-up value. Those represent different valuation concepts; DCF terminal value is the discounted present value of all post-forecast cash flows treated as a perpetuity (or via an exit multiple).
